model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) of six different methods—labeled Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on the x-axis using a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to 10³ (1000) with tick marks at intervals of 10¹ (10), 10² (100), and 10³ (1000). The y-axis represents ACC as a percentage, ranging from 40% to 65%, with tick marks at 5% intervals. The Base method, shown as a black line with circular markers, starts at approximately 38% ACC at a co-occurrence number of 0 and rises to about 44% at 1000, remaining relatively flat after that. The MEND method, depicted as a brown line with diamond markers, begins at around 44% ACC and steadily increases to approximately 57% at 1000. The FT method, shown as a blue line with triangle markers, starts at about 40% ACC and increases to roughly 47% at 1000. The MEMIT method, represented by a purple line with star markers, begins at approximately 44% ACC and rises to about 55% at 1000. The IKE method, shown as a red line with triangle markers, starts at roughly 43% ACC and increases to about 50% at 1000. The ROME method, depicted as a green line with square markers, starts at approximately 51% ACC and rises sharply to about 65% at 1000.
